author: pi-agent

patch.value: Reproduced on this host: rustup default stable resolved to 1.86.0 and cargo test failed immediately with a rustc-not-supported error naming pm-rust 0.1.0-alpha.1 eight times plus time 0.3.55 and time-core 0.1.9. Running the identical tree under cargo plus-1.90.0 passed all 26 tests across 5 test binaries.
A green CI proves nothing about a working copy, because the toolchain is pinned only inside the workflows

Cargo.toml declares rust-version 1.90 as a minimum and the two GitHub workflows install 1.90.0 explicitly in three places, but the repository carries no rust-toolchain.toml. rustup therefore selects whichever toolchain the contributor default resolves to. On a host whose stable channel resolved to 1.86.0, cargo test aborted with a rustc-not-supported error before compiling anything, while CI stayed green because it installs its own toolchain. The build requirement was real but discoverable only by reading the workflows.

A rust-toolchain.toml at the crate root selects 1.90.0 so rustup uses the same compiler locally that CI installs; cargo test succeeds on a host whose default stable toolchain is older than 1.90 without a plus-toolchain override; The pinned channel matches the toolchain values in ci.yml and release.yml

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Found while verifying every fleet package builds on this host rather than trusting CI status. pm-rust was the only package that could not be built or tested locally at all.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Cargo rust-version is a minimum-version assertion, not a toolchain selector. Only rust-toolchain.toml makes rustup choose a compiler.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: A minimum-version declaration and a toolchain pin are different mechanisms; only the latter makes local and CI agree, and CI cannot detect the difference because it always installs its own.

message: Track the local-versus-CI toolchain divergence found while verifying pm-rust on this host
